I think the FZ criteria are super high in any language class. However, Chinese is fun and more manageable than other European language classes (In Chinese, you do not need to memorize the conjugation of verbs, and all the exams are prepared in pinyin so there is no need to learn all Chinese characters.) 
Some advice to students that want to take this course:
Be prepared for the first midterm/written exam so you don't get an FZ. The listening exam is easier.  
If you do not have time to exclusively study for Chinese, take notes in class. That already counts as practice.  
If you happen to miss a class, be sure to look at all sources on Moodle (they are updated weekly)
Although, you do not need to memorize Chinese characters that much, there are common words you have to recognize. Writing them on a piece of paper a few times usually helps. (If you already have vocab memorization techniques, that will also work.)
